\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{মুলতুবি} (multubi)}{মুলতুবি (multubi)}]{\bn{মুলতুবি} (multubi) — adjourned; put off}

\label{lesson:BN-C530-multubi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to lean forward, then the Bengali for a whim.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{মুলতুবি}}
\textbf{\bn{মুলতুবি}} — \emph{multubi} — \textquotedblleft{}adjourned; put off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ঝড়} \bn{হলে} \bn{মিটিং} \bn{মুলতুবি} \bn{হবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Jhôṛ hôle miṭing multubi hôbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If there is a storm, the meeting will be put off.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{মুলতুবি}} (\emph{multubi}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{multawī}, \textquotedblleft{}deferred\textquotedblright{}, through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{multubi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{multubi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Jhôṛ hôle miṭing multubi hôbe.} — If there is a storm, the meeting will be put off.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to lean forward, then the Bengali for a whim, then say \emph{multubi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{মুলতুবি} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Adjourned; put off\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{নির্দিষ্ট} (nirdishṭô)}{নির্দিষ্ট (nirdishṭô)}]{\bn{নির্দিষ্ট} (nirdishṭô) — fixed; set; particular}

\label{lesson:BN-C530-nirdishto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a whim, then the Bengali for adjourned.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{নির্দিষ্ট}}
\textbf{\bn{নির্দিষ্ট}} — \emph{nirdishṭô} — \textquotedblleft{}fixed; set; particular\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{প্রতি} \bn{মাসের} \bn{একটা} \bn{নির্দিষ্ট} \bn{দিনে} \bn{আমি} \bn{ভাড়া} \bn{দিই।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Prôti māser ekṭā nirdishṭô dine āmi bhāṛā dii.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I pay the rent on a fixed day every month.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{নির্দিষ্ট}} (\emph{nirdishṭô}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{nirdiṣṭa}, \textquotedblleft{}pointed out, specified\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nirdishṭô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Prôti māser ekṭā nirdishṭô dine āmi bhāṛā dii.} — I pay the rent on a fixed day every month.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a whim, then the Bengali for adjourned, then say \emph{nirdishṭô} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{আগাম} (āgām)}{আগাম (āgām)}]{\bn{আগাম} (āgām) — in advance; an advance}

\label{lesson:BN-C530-agam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for adjourned, then the Bengali for fixed in advance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{আগাম}}
\textbf{\bn{আগাম}} — \emph{āgām} — \textquotedblleft{}in advance; an advance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{আগাম} \bn{টাকা} \bn{দিলে} \bn{হোটেল} \bn{আমাদের} \bn{জন্য} \bn{ঘর} \bn{রাখবে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Āgām ṭākā dile hoṭel āmāder jônyô ghôr rākhbe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If we pay in advance, the hotel will keep a room for us.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{আগাম}} (\emph{āgām}) is built on \bn{আগ}, \textquotedblleft{}the front\textquotedblright{}, from Sanskrit \emph{agra} (CDIAL 68), the root of \bn{আগে}, \textquotedblleft{}before\textquotedblright{}; how the ending arose is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āgām}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Āgām ṭākā dile hoṭel āmāder jônyô ghôr rākhbe.} — If we pay in advance, the hotel will keep a room for us.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for adjourned, then the Bengali for fixed in advance, then say \emph{āgām} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{টালবাহানা} \bn{করা} (ṭālbāhānā kôrā)}{টালবাহানা করা (ṭālbāhānā kôrā)}]{\bn{টালবাহানা} \bn{করা} (ṭālbāhānā kôrā) — to stall; to keep making excuses}

\label{lesson:BN-C530-talbahana-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for fixed in advance, then the Bengali for in advance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{টালবাহানা} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{টালবাহানা} \bn{করা}} — \emph{ṭālbāhānā kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to stall; to keep making excuses\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{দোকানদার} \bn{টাকা} \bn{ফিরিয়ে} \bn{দিতে} \bn{টালবাহানা} \bn{করল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dokāndār ṭākā phiriye dite ṭālbāhānā kôrlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shopkeeper kept stalling about giving the money back.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{সই} \bn{করতে} \bn{টালবাহানা} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini sôi kôrte ṭālbāhānā kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{টালবাহানা} \bn{করা}} (\emph{ṭālbāhānā kôrā}) joins \bn{টাল}, \textquotedblleft{}evasion\textquotedblright{}, from the family of \emph{ṭalati}, \textquotedblleft{}moves aside\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 5450, which lists Bengali \emph{ṭālā}, \textquotedblleft{}to evade\textquotedblright{}), and \bn{বাহানা}, \textquotedblleft{}a pretext\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Persian \emph{bahāna}, to \bn{করা}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সাব্যস্ত} \bn{করা} (sābyôstô kôrā)}{সাব্যস্ত করা (sābyôstô kôrā)}]{\bn{সাব্যস্ত} \bn{করা} (sābyôstô kôrā) — to settle on; to decide finally}

\label{lesson:BN-C530-sabyosto-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for in advance, then the Bengali for to stall.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সাব্যস্ত} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{সাব্যস্ত} \bn{করা}} — \emph{sābyôstô kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to settle on; to decide finally\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{অনেক} \bn{ভেবে} \bn{আমরা} \bn{শুক্রবার} \bn{যাওয়া} \bn{সাব্যস্ত} \bn{করলাম।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ônek bhebe āmrā shukrôbār jāoyā sābyôstô kôrlām.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After much thought we settled on going on Friday.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{তারিখটা} \bn{সাব্যস্ত} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini tārikhṭā sābyôstô kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সাব্যস্ত} \bn{করা}} (\emph{sābyôstô kôrā}) joins \bn{সাব্যস্ত}, \textquotedblleft{}established, settled\textquotedblright{}, to \bn{করা}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}. \bn{সাব্যস্ত} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{thābit}, \textquotedblleft{}firm\textquotedblright{}, through Persian \emph{sābit}; how its ending arose is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}
